full_judgment: 11. Considering the submissions of the learned Advocates, I have perused the application for pre-emption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 wherein it has been clearly contended by the pre-emptor-petitioner that the case land was transferred by a saf-kabala deed dated 28-5-2012 and the land measuring 10 decimals was transferred, in favour of the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1, who is a stranger purchaser at a consideration of Taka 3,00,000 (Taka three lac). The certified copy of the application for pre-emption is annexed herewith as Annexure-`A'. I have also consulted the application under Order VII, rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil' Procedure wherein it was cited by the opposite party No. 1 that the case land being a non-agricultural land and homestead the preemption miscellaneous case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 is not maintainable. With regard to this, having gone through the order passed by the trial court dated 1-9-2015 in pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 25 of 2012 and the order of the appellate court dated 30-9-2015 in Miscellaneous Appeal No.64 of 2015 it transpires that the learned District Judge, Barisal held that in the SA Khatian the land transferred, was mentioned as `Bhiti' and `Bagan' and for that reason it can be held that the land is not an agricultural land.
